Create the file case_120.inp in the working directory containing exactly the input deck provided in the task, byte-for-byte, with no modifications to the physics, keywords, sets, or numbering.
Verify that ccx is available by running ccx -v (or the closest equivalent) and record the version string printed by that command.
Run the CalculiX analysis using the command ccx -i case_120; if that fails or is not supported on the installed version, run ccx case_120 instead.
Do not modify the input deck, add steps, loads, or outputs, or rerun with different parameters if the run completes.

Create a results.json file in the working directory with the fields: solver set to "calculix", case_id set to "case_120", status set to "success" if the run terminated successfully or "error" otherwise, ccx_version set to the version string obtained from ccx -v, artifacts set to an empty list, and notes containing the exact ccx command used.
If the run fails, additionally include in notes the exact error message and the name of the file that indicated the failure (e.g., case_120.sta, case_120.cvg, or the .dat/.sta output showing the error).
Leave all generated CalculiX output files (case_120.frd, case_120.dat, case_120.sta, and any others) in the working directory as artifacts of the run.
